title: Where Will the 2027 Total Solar Eclipse Last Over Six Minutes?
description:
Where Will the 2027 Total Solar Eclipse Last Over Six Minutes?

On 2 August 2027, the Moon's umbral shadow—up to 258 kilometres wide—will sweep across southern Spain and North Africa, peaking over central Egypt at 6 minutes and 23 seconds of totality, nearly triple 2026's two-minute total solar eclipse.

Sources: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center Eclipse Predictions by Fred Espenak (2027 Aug 02 Total Solar Eclipse; greatest duration 06m23.2s in central Egypt at 26°49'N 31°08'E; greatest eclipse 06m22.6s east of Luxor; path width up to 258 km across Spain, Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt, Saudi Arabia; 2026 Aug 12 total eclipse 02m18s).
https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/SEgoogle/SEgoogle2001/SE2027Aug02Tgoogle.html
https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/SEpath/SEpath2001/SE2027Aug02Tpath.html
https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/SEdecade/SEdecade2021.html

Pictures: NASA, NOAA, ESA, and ESO imagery alongside our own code-drawn 2027 eclipse path map and animated graphics. Facts: every number is checked against the sources above.
Image credits: NASA; NASA/Aubrey Gemignani; NASA/GSFC; NOAA; ESA – European Space Agency / A. Gerst (CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO); R. Wesson/ESO (CC BY 4.0).
